summary: Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He taught at Komazawa University from circa 1930 to 1970.

Reiko Ohnuma works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini, later holding posts at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. His career included posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and Ryukoku University.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig, where he served as assistant professor from 1832 and extraordinary professor from 1849 to 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, and served on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Johann Gustav Stickel and Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and the India Office.
Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College.
Remeen Firoz is an Indologist who has been a PhD student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Renate Syed is an Indologist who completed her doctorate at the University of Munich under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She is attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Renjo Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
Renshan Yang was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Jinling Scriptural Press and the Jetavana Hermitage. In 1910, he founded and headed the Buddhist Research Society.
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the University of Helsinki, where he also held an academic post from circa 1975 to 2014.

René Grousset was a historian and scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Montpellier, he held positions at the Guimet Museum, École du Louvre, Musée Cernuschi, and the Louvre.
René Guénon was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He completed his education at the Robert-Badinter School Complex, Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour, and the University of Paris.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz was a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna, SOAS, LSE, and Humboldt University, working under teachers including Tucci and Rock, and served at the Weltmuseum Wien in 1958.
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi was an Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he later served as Head of Sahityavidya from circa 1977 to 1995.
Rewata Dhamma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and completed a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University.

Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University (circa 1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (circa 1978–2010).
